target.label: 8b moonshot · short-context ITL
target.why: the card's measured ceiling: 16.36 GB/token at 149 GB/s, one fp16 matmul across all 32 cores

moved.what: rung-1 prompts re-measured at calibrated length. The first pass's prompts recorded 1.5× their buckets server-side (207/1614/15209 for 128/1061/10091) — a client words-per-token heuristic, not code — and those cells are discarded. The re-measured cells (the 10-18 prompt texts; serve-recorded 128/1061/10091 per rep) show no rung-1 regression: see #667 and #641. The fp8 rung-1 squares land with them (8b fp8 TTFT 190 → 149.9 ms).

CB-submission ports, batch-chunk query groups and batch K/V gather in LX make the batch rungs measurable: this sweep adds the page's first fp16 batched cells. Conc 4 lands at parity with torch-spyre (2b ~1k ITL 64.8 vs 67.7 ms; 8b ~1k 161.3 vs 160.1 ms); conc 8 runs behind (8b ~1k 199.3 vs 173.9 ms; 38.4 vs 45.0 tok/s).

prefill causal mask staged once per key. The re-measured rung-1 TTFT cells improved at every bucket on the same harness (2b 81 → 67.5 ms at ~123, 636 → 561 ms at ~1k, 8.15 → 7.76 s at ~10k; 8b 12.8 → 12.3 s at ~10k) — the sweep-over-sweep delta across #621–#668, not this PR alone.

8b Kᵗ kept in LX on the 8-page rung: the 10-18 lever projected ≈−23 ms/step at 8b ~10k; the re-measured cell is 154.6 ms against 10-18's 179.7 on the same harness — −25.0 ms/step, on the projection (sweep-over-sweep across #621–#668).
replay counter — telemetry for compile-time CB replay; no cell claim.
prefix-rung bake guard (guard only) and the MoE prefill kernel (not wired into this build) — no cell claims.

levers.work: 131.1 ms at ~123 against the card's ≈110 ms floor (16.4 GB/token at 149 GB/s) — the rest is attention and elementwise glue.
2b conc-8 ~10k ITL 1178.9 ms vs torch 370.1 (3.2×); the 8b batched ~10k cells are absent by design — the KV budget at max-model-len 34816 fits ≤2 concurrent seqs.

8b ~1k: torch-spyre 1.15× ahead (ITL 173.9 vs 199.3 ms; 45.0 vs 38.4 tok/s); 2b near parity (88.9 vs 91.1 ms; 86.4 vs 84.1 tok/s). Batched TTFT is the wider gap: 2b conc-8 ~1k 1170 vs 464 ms, 8b 2546 vs 790 ms.

149.9 ms at ~123 — 11% under this sweep's fp16 (168.2) and 21% under 10-18's fp8 (190): the halved weight bytes now beat the per-row quantize overhead, but only just; fusing the quantize into the matmul is still the work.
2b fp8 short-context ITL is 27.2 ms; ~10% of it is host time between steps — compile-time CB replay with the next token chosen on the device (#603).

decode: Short-context parity is a shared floor: both stacks stream 16.4 GB of fp16 weights per token. Measured on the card (17 Oct), one fp16 matmul streams at most ~149 GB/s, and only across all 32 cores — the cost model's 204.8 GB/s peak is not reachable — so fp16 at one request bottoms out near 110 ms/token.

The fp16 rung-1 (single-request) cells are the calibrated re-measure (#677): the first pass's prompts recorded 1.5× their buckets server-side (207/1614/15209 for 128/1061/10091 — a client words-per-token heuristic, not code), so those cells were discarded and the legs re-run with the tokenizer-calibrated client sending the 10-18 sweep's own prompt texts; the serve recorded 128/1061/10091 per rep, gated to ±2%. The fp8 rung-1 squares are that same re-measure, run on nickm2: 2b ITL 27.20 ms (10-18: 26.19) and 8b 73.97 (72.61) — flat. The batched cells are unaffected — both stacks ran vllm bench on the same conc-* sets.
prefill: The fp16 rung-1 TTFT squares are the calibrated re-measure (#677; serve-recorded 128/1061/10091 per rep). Against 2026-10-18 on the same harness they improved at every bucket — 2b 81 → 67.5 ms at ~123, 636 → 561 ms at ~1k, 8.15 → 7.76 s at ~10k; 8b 12.8 → 12.3 s at ~10k — so the first pass's apparent prefill regression was the prompt-length artifact, not code. The fp8 rung-1 TTFT squares are the same re-measure on nickm2: 8b fp8 149.9 ms (10-18: 190) — 21% better and 11% under this sweep's fp16 168.2 — and the first 2b fp8 TTFT cell, 67.9 ms. The batched TTFT cells stand — both sides ran the same conc-* sets.
conc: Every batched cell is the second of two back-to-back reps on one server boot (rep 1 is reliably the slow rep — TTFT ~6–7 s vs ~2.6 s, a property of the harness); both reps are recorded in each cell's note. Decode squares prefer itl_ms (per-request median TPOT under that batch); tok_s is recorded alongside for the concurrency view. The 2026-10-18 conc-8 cells recorded no rep convention (a single bench after two warmups), so this sweep's conc-8 ~1k cells are stated against torch, never as cross-sweep deltas.

The 8b fp16 batched ~10k squares are unmeasured by design: the serve refuses at boot — max-model-len 34816 × max-num-seqs 4 needs 545 KV pages (32700 MB at 60 MB per page) against the 16384 MB budget (273 pages); at max-num-seqs 8 it needs 1089 pages (65340 MB). 8b ~10k at this max-model-len fits ≤2 concurrent seqs; left absent rather than re-run at a smaller max-model-len, which would make the cell non-like-for-like with its row.

Three legs are left out rather than carrying old numbers, all on the torch side. t4/t8-8b-8-123 (8b fp8 conc): the serve boot exceeds the harness's 900 s ready window — attention-graph recording alone took 428.7 s and the serve was healthy, just slow — so both stripe pending a re-run with a longer window. t8-8b-16-123: the re-run died to RAS::VFIO::DeviceOpenFail 0x332b ("Device or resource busy" — Failed to open the IBM Spyre VFIO device) because the timed-out 8b fp8 serve had not released /dev/vfio/54 when this serve opened it; its first attempt died to a PCIe bus fence (RAS::PCI::BusFence 0xa35e; the card recovered and the following leg booted clean). The 2b fp8 torch legs landed on nickm4 (t1/t4/t8-2b-8-123). All land in a follow-up to this same file (same sha, same harness — one sweep).
fp8: The fp8 rung-1 squares (2b/8b at ~123) are the #677 calibrated re-measure on nickm2 (serve-recorded 128 per rep): 2b 27.20 ms ITL / 67.9 ms TTFT (the first 2b fp8 TTFT cell), 8b 73.97 / 149.9. On the torch side the 2b fp8 legs landed on nickm4 — rung-1 ITL 260.1 ms, ~9.6× scratchy's 27.2 — while the 8b fp8 conc squares sit in the concurrency notes' pending set (serve boots exceed the ready window).
